A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MergePrint and retain the same central formulation. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, supporting comparison despite substantial rewriting and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original fingerprint-verification, harmlessness and optimization experiments, including LLaMA-2 merging results and Mistral experiments and parameter-distance analysis in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original merging and harmlessness experiments, together with confidentiality, parameter-modification, hyperparameter, fingerprint-output and multiple-fingerprint evaluations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains GCG input optimization with base-model regularization, followed by parameter optimization through a pseudo-merged model. Equations 5–7 are equivalent across versions after matching notation. v2 adds pseudocode and implementation details; its multiple-fingerprint experiments apply the existing method without establishing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 replaces StrongReject-small safety evaluation with ToxiGen, removes SquadCompletion, adds Japanese QA and mathematics evaluation through JAQKET and MGSM, and uses Alpaca for fine-tuning attacks. Coverage expands to pruning, quantization, fingerprint overwriting and altered inference conditions. LLaMA-2 and Mistral experiments were already present in v1.

E2.justification: TRAP joins IF as a fingerprinting baseline, adding an intrinsic-fingerprint comparator throughout major evaluations. IF also enters the harmlessness comparison, where v1 compared only the original model and MergePrint variants. The retained Abel–Shisa merging experiments gain both IF and TRAP comparisons; v1 Tables 9 and 11 reported only MergePrint.

E3.justification: Equation 8 changes the documented VSR success condition from output containment to exact-prefix matching. The embedding learning rate changes from 1e-6 in v1 Section 5.5 to 1e-7 in v2 Appendix A.1.1. v2 adds Breadcrumbs and DELLA merging protocols and new attack settings, including three-epoch Alpaca fine-tuning. The earlier Mistral WizardMath pairing suite is omitted.

E4.justification: v2 retains the input-optimization ablation but adds substantial analyses of regularization and merge coefficients, target-output types and lengths, embedding up to 20 fingerprints, character replacement, pruning and generation parameters. These test sensitivity, interference and robustness beyond v1's analyses. Conversely, v1 Appendix C.2's parameter-distance investigation and its supporting distance table are removed.

E5.justification: v2 specifies 30 trials for character-replacement averages, three trials for output-choice results and five independent trials for random pruning. Table 7 introduces plus/minus reporting, although the statistic represented is not explicitly identified. This is a limited expansion beyond v1's VSR and across-task difference statistics, without documenting increased runs for retained main experiments.

E6.justification: Many results are replaced or added. For fingerprinted WizardMath merged with LLaMA-2-CHAT using Task Arithmetic without DARE at alpha=0.5, IF's reported VSR changes from 1.00 in v1 Table 1 to 0.08 in v2 Table 9. Changed protocols prevent interpreting this as a same-setting decline. v2 adds extensive attack, sensitivity, harmlessness and timing results while removing the parameter-distance results.

T1.justification: Equation 8 revises VSR's mathematical event from the target appearing in the generated response to equality with its first target-length tokens. The pseudo-merged-model definition and optimization objectives remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs whose substance changes.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly places fine-tuning outside scope, whereas v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion claim resistance to broader model-theft threats, including fine-tuning, pruning and quantization. The introduction also adds concrete sub-ten-minute efficiency and stronger confidentiality claims. The original claim of merge-resistant fingerprinting with black-box ownership verification is retained.

C2.justification: v1's parameter-distance explanation and associated future-work caveat disappear. v2 instead argues that fingerprint loss is not a vulnerability when merging also loses owner-model utility. It adds explanations of target-output failures and an explicit knowledge-distillation limitation. Membership inference changes from an acknowledged potential vulnerability in v1 to an attack characterized as highly impractical in v2.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation with Algorithm 1, regularization and stopping thresholds, 32-token inputs, GCG batch size and candidate settings, iteration limits, baseline details and single-A100 timing information. Section 10 adds a supplemental-code and planned public-release statement. However, Appendix A.1.1's stopping-direction prose contradicts the main text and pseudocode.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially rewritten around white-box versus black-box verification and intrinsic versus injected fingerprints. v2 adds discussion of HuReF, REEF, TRAP, functional-invariant watermarking and BadMerging. It removes v1's output-watermarking discussion and Cong et al.'s directly relevant model-merging robustness study, changing the positioning of the research gap.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, threat-model discussion and method exposition. Related work becomes a standalone section, the method gains three subsections, six requirements become five, and limitations move after the conclusion. The appendices are reorganized, with new ethics and reproducibility sections. Title and author-order changes accompany this substantial narrative revision.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, replaces the main merging table with an eight-panel plot and presents revised detailed matrices in the appendices. It redesigns the response example and plots and adds pseudocode, a heatmap and numerous analysis displays. v1 Table 2 becomes v2 Table 1 through reformatting and rounding, rather than representing a new experiment.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited validation and sparse implementation reporting. TRAP comparisons, hyperparameter and output-choice studies, multiple-fingerprint tests and broader attack evaluations strengthen assessment of the unchanged method, while detailed settings and pseudocode improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the loss of the parameter-distance study and reporting weaknesses. Nevertheless, the character-replacement experiment does not establish the stronger extraction-resistance claims, and the inconsistent stopping-direction prose remains a concrete defect.
